title: Bridging Tokens and Geometry: Token-wise 3D Supervision for CAD Generation
claim: Prior methods add visual inputs or only sequence-level rendered feedback; ours gives dense token-wise geometric supervision by lifting tokens to 3D points.
layout: 3 panels: large left (ours), two stacked right (prior), vertical divider
description: The figure compares three ways of bringing visual information into CAD sequence generation. The large left panel (a), the proposed method, shows inputs (image, point cloud, text) feeding grammar-constrained generation of a CAD sequence. Colored argument tokens are connected by blue lines through point lifting to 3D points on a predicted 3D part. An L2 loss compares these points with the label shape, and a big gray arrow shows the supervision. The top-right panel (b) is a simple box diagram: prompt and visual inputs go into a model that outputs a CAD program. The bottom-right panel (c) is a reinforcement-style loop: the model samples a CAD program, which is rendered and compared with ground truth to compute a reward and optimize the policy. The eye goes first to the detailed left panel with the 3D shapes.

abstract: Computer-Aided Design (CAD) generation is typically formulated as a sequence modeling task over parametric tokens. Recent studies introduce visual information through additional visual inputs or rendering of the final generated programs. However, these methods provide no intermediate visual feedback, hindering the association of individual tokens with their geometric effects. In this work, we propose an Argument-induced 3D Point Loss (A3PL) that maps argument tokens to corresponding 3D points, enabling dense token-wise geometric supervision. To reduce learning complexity and invalid sequences, we further introduce a Grammar-constrained Operator (GCO) that leverages the structured nature of CAD programs to regulate sequence generation. We evaluate our approach on five CAD generation tasks with diverse input modalities, including text, Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) sketches, point clouds, and CAD sequences. Our approach improves generation accuracy and program validity across different input modalities. Code is available at https://github.com/JumpJumpTigger-GYJ/A3PL.
